 Roberts to Present Senior Art Exhibit
 41 minutes ago • November 17, 2026 
 By Larry Isch 
 Posted in Art 
 University of the Ozarks senior Stacie R. Roberts of Hector, Ark., will present her music-inspired Senior Art Exhibit, Visual Sounds of Emotion , from Nov. 16-20, in the Stephens Art Gallery.
 There will be a reception to meet the artist from 7-8 p.m. on Nov. 20.
 An art major who will graduate with Summa Cum Laude honors next month, Roberts is a graduate of Dover (Ark.) High School.
 Roberts said Visual Sounds of Emotion explores how music interacts with humans’ emotional responses through whimsical worlds and cartoonish characters contrasted against realistic and personal artworks. Roberts’ choice to pursue this combination of fine arts and music stems from her family’s vast history of artists and musicians, and especially from her grandparents’ direct influence on her talents.
 “My exhibition features three series representing emotion through a musical lens in different ways: realistic, personal experiences; the general experience and emotional power of music; and representations of emotion itself,” Roberts said. “The realistic series showcases several pieces related to my own life. Try New Things showcases four different guitars—three acoustic guitars and a single electric guitar—representative of my family’s long history with music. Each of the acoustic guitars once belonged to a different family member who has since passed, while the electric guitar is originally mine. The electric guitar stands out against the brown acoustic guitars and the wooden background as new, shiny, and exciting; Exactly how I had felt to have the opportunity to finally learn to play the guitar.”
 Roberts said several of her pieces are in a style reminiscent of 1920s and 30s rubberhose animations.
 “This style appeals to my idea of the complexity of emotions in a style that is bouncy and unserious in appearance while the actual content is much more serious,” she said. “My cup-headed characters represent the general population’s emotional experiences, and how easily human emotions are influenced by, and tend to influence, the world around us. These cartoonish worlds and characters reflect how emotions may appear one way at a glance, but are much more complex whenever you actually start to look deeper. My painted guitar sculpture, Irrational Fear of Change, shows two different ways of looking at the world: The back is a scene of a cup-headed character cowering in fear from an evil devil, while the front is a peaceful, sunny hillside with a pair of flowers. I specifically chose to display this piece backwards so the viewer feels inclined to walk around to see the front of the guitar. It is a simple motion indicative of how easy a change can be if we seek it, even if at first it feels frightening.”
 Roberts added that in between these two ends of a spectrum from whimsy to realism, her final series of headphone drawings “represents raw, unfiltered emotions ranging from calm to boiled-over frustrations and rage.”
 “Each one uses bold, vivid colors reflective of the emotions they show. The way these pieces are arranged on the wall is representative of how fragile our emotional balance can be, and how quickly emotions can shift in either direction, positive or negative. These pieces are seated at the center of my layout, and the center of my concepts.”
 Roberts also showed her artwork in the Applied Research and Creative Highlights (ARCH) Symposium in 2026, for which she was awarded a second-place prize for her piece, Out With The Old.
